quests.question: Sixty percent of the voters ___ in favor of the proposal.
quests.hint: Look at the noun right after 'of' - is it one countable thing or many?
quests.explanation: 'The voters' is a countable plural noun, so the percentage expression behaves like a plural subject. The verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + plural noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: About forty percent of the employees ___ from home twice a week.
quests.hint: 'Employees' is a plural, countable noun - let that guide your choice of verb.
quests.explanation: Since 'employees' is plural and countable, the percentage takes a plural verb: 'work'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + plural noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: Nearly ninety percent of the students ___ the assignment on time.
quests.hint: Check whether 'students' can be counted one by one - that decides the verb form.
quests.explanation: 'Students' is plural and countable, so the verb stays in the base form: 'submit'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + plural noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: Sixty percent of the cake ___ already gone.
quests.hint: This time, look at 'the cake' - can you count it the same way you'd count people?
quests.explanation: 'Cake' is uncountable here (thought of as one whole dessert), so the percentage takes a singular verb: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + singular/uncountable noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: About twenty percent of the budget ___ toward marketing.
quests.hint: 'The budget' is treated as one single amount, not a group of countable items.
quests.explanation: 'Budget' is singular here, so the percentage takes a singular verb: 'goes'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + singular/uncountable noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Nearly half of the water in this reservoir ___ from melted snow.
quests.hint: 'Water' can't be counted one by one - think about what that means for the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Water' is uncountable, so 'nearly half of the water' takes a singular verb: 'comes'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + singular/uncountable noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Two-thirds of the pizza ___ already eaten.
quests.hint: 'Pizza' isn't usually counted individually - think of it as one whole item here.
quests.explanation: 'Pizza' is uncountable in this sense, so the fraction takes a singular verb: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Fraction + 'of' + noun agrees with the noun after 'of'

quests.question: Two-thirds of the students ___ part-time jobs.
quests.hint: Compare this to the pizza example - 'students' can definitely be counted one by one.
quests.explanation: 'Students' is countable and plural, so the fraction takes a plural verb: 'have'.
quests.grammarRule: Fraction + 'of' + noun agrees with the noun after 'of'

quests.question: One-quarter of the applicants ___ prior experience in this field.
quests.hint: 'Applicants' is just as countable as 'students' - apply the same logic.
quests.explanation: 'Applicants' is plural and countable, so the verb stays in the base form: 'lack'.
quests.grammarRule: Fraction + 'of' + noun agrees with the noun after 'of'

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Ten dollars ___ a fair price for this used book.
quests.hint: Ten dollars is being described as one total price, not as ten separate coins.
quests.explanation: When money is thought of as a single sum, it's singular. The verb here is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Money expressed as a single total amount takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Two hundred dollars ___ enough to cover the repair.
quests.hint: Think of '$200' as one lump sum needed for the repair.
quests.explanation: 'Two hundred dollars' refers to one total amount, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: Money expressed as a single total amount takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Fifty euros ___ more than I expected to pay for entry.
quests.hint: This amount is being talked about as a single price, not as fifty separate coins.
quests.explanation: 'Fifty euros' is one overall amount here, so the verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Money expressed as a single total amount takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Two years ___ a long time to wait for results.
quests.hint: Two years here is one stretch of waiting, not two separate units being counted.
quests.explanation: A span of time is usually treated as one period, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Time expressed as a single duration takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Six months ___ enough time to learn the basics.
quests.hint: Six months is being described as one length of time to learn something.
quests.explanation: 'Six months' is a single duration here, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: Time expressed as a single duration takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Three hours ___ too long for this meeting.
quests.hint: Three hours describes one overall length for the meeting, not three separate hours being counted.
quests.explanation: 'Three hours' is treated as a single duration, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Time expressed as a single duration takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Five miles ___ a reasonable distance to bike each day.
quests.hint: Five miles here describes one overall distance, not five separate miles being counted.
quests.explanation: A distance is usually treated as one single measurement, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Distance or weight expressed as a single measurement takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Ten kilograms ___ too heavy for this shelf to hold.
quests.hint: Ten kilograms is being described as one total weight for the shelf to support.
quests.explanation: 'Ten kilograms' is a single measurement here, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: Distance or weight expressed as a single measurement takes a singular verb

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Two hundred meters ___ the length of the new bridge.
quests.hint: Two hundred meters is one overall length, not two hundred separate meters being counted.
quests.explanation: 'Two hundred meters' is treated as a single measurement, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Distance or weight expressed as a single measurement takes a singular verb

quests.question: A number of employees ___ requested a schedule change.
quests.hint: 'A number of' means roughly 'several' - treat the whole phrase as plural.
quests.explanation: 'A number of employees' means 'several employees', so it takes a plural verb: 'have'.
quests.grammarRule: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: The number of employees ___ increasing steadily this year.
quests.hint: 'The number of' refers to the count itself - one single figure, so it's singular.
quests.explanation: 'The number of employees' refers to a single figure or statistic, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: A number of complaints ___ under review.
quests.hint: This phrase means 'several complaints' - apply the plural rule from earlier in this level.
quests.explanation: 'A number of complaints' means 'several complaints', so the verb stays in the base form: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: A couple of chairs ___ still missing from the set.
quests.hint: Phrases like 'a couple of' work like quantifiers - they take their number from the noun that follows.
quests.explanation: 'A couple of chairs' behaves like 'two chairs', so the verb is plural: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Quantifier expressions ('a couple of', 'a dozen of', 'a handful of') agree with the noun after 'of'

quests.question: A dozen of the applicants ___ scheduled for interviews next week.
quests.hint: 'A dozen of' behaves the same way as 'a couple of' - check the noun after 'of'.
quests.explanation: 'A dozen of the applicants' behaves like 'twelve applicants', so the verb is plural: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Quantifier expressions ('a couple of', 'a dozen of', 'a handful of') agree with the noun after 'of'

quests.question: A handful of volunteers ___ helping with the cleanup.
quests.hint: 'A handful of' also takes its number from the noun that follows it.
quests.explanation: 'A handful of volunteers' behaves like 'several volunteers', so the verb is plural: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Quantifier expressions ('a couple of', 'a dozen of', 'a handful of') agree with the noun after 'of'

quests.question: Seventy-five percent of the reports submitted this quarter ___ under review.
quests.hint: Trace past the description of when the reports were submitted and apply the percentage rule.
quests.explanation: 'Seventy-five percent of the reports' is plural because 'reports' is countable; 'submitted this quarter' is just extra detail. The verb stays in the base form: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + plural noun stays plural, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.question: The number of accidents on this highway ___ every year.
quests.hint: Focus on 'the number of', not the highway description that follows.
quests.explanation: 'The number of accidents' is singular, since it refers to a single count; 'on this highway' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'decreases'.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.question: A number of issues raised during the meeting ___ unresolved.
quests.hint: This phrase still means 'several issues', even with the extra description in between.
quests.explanation: 'A number of issues' is plural; 'raised during the meeting' is just extra detail. The verb stays in the base form: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.question: Nearly half of the cookies ___ gone before the party even started.
quests.hint: Bring back the percentage/fraction rule: check whether 'cookies' can be counted individually.
quests.explanation: 'Cookies' is countable and plural, so 'nearly half of the cookies' takes a plural verb: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage or fraction + 'of' + plural noun takes a plural verb

quests.question: Twenty dollars ___ too much to spend on a single meal.
quests.hint: Remember: an amount of money described as one total sum is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Twenty dollars' is treated as one total amount, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: Money expressed as a single total amount takes a singular verb

quests.question: The number of visitors ___ every summer.
quests.hint: As a final check, recall that 'the number of' always refers to one single count.
quests.explanation: 'The number of visitors' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'rises'.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
